title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (recapitulated in §6 of this page). Data I: X is a scheme of finite type over Q̄. D = Σ_{i∈I} D_i is an effective divisor whose components are (probably) required to be smooth or irreducible, with X smooth at the generic (maximal) points of supp D. X' = X − D, and J ⊂ X'(Q̄) is a chosen set of rational points.

Derived data II:
- 𝒢' is the group of automorphisms of the scheme X (not necessarily Q̄-linear, hence semilinear) preserving D and J.
- G' ⊂ 𝒢' is the subgroup of Q̄-automorphisms.
- T(Q̄) = lim μ_n(Q̄) = Ẑ(1).
- Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q).
- The next page gives 1 → G' → 𝒢' → Γ, with image open after restricting to some Γ' ⊂ Γ.

Choosing a universal pro-étale cover X̃' → X' with π_1 = Aut(X̃'/X') gives an extension 1 → π_1(X') → E' → 𝒢' → 1. Here E' consists of the automorphisms of X̃' lifting elements of 𝒢', i.e. the preimage of 𝒢' ⊂ 𝒢_{X'} in E_{X'}. It is an 'arithmetic fundamental group enlarged by the geometric symmetries'.

Previous page: the 'points at infinity' X̃'(i) over each D_i give inertia homomorphisms φ_i: T(Q̄) → π_1(X'). These are compatible with E' acting on X̃'(I), on π_1 by conjugation, and on Ẑ(1) via Γ (cyclotomic twist). This is divisorial inertia, i.e. the cusps.

This page, formula (25): for each j ∈ J, with 𝒢'_j the stabilizer of j in 𝒢', there is a map Ψ_j: X̃'(j) → Hom(𝒢'_j, E'). It sends a point x̃ above j to the unique section 𝒢'_j → E' whose image fixes x̃. This works because π_1 acts simply transitively on the fibre over j, so each g ∈ 𝒢'_j has exactly one lift fixing x̃. The family Ψ = (Ψ_j) is E'-equivariant: e acts on X̃'(J) by translation and on Hom by conjugation (on E' by e, on 𝒢'_j by the image of e). These are the 'scindages partiels'.

A crossed-out attempt (26) introduced an extended family Ψ^ext involving the whole 𝒢' (or π_1(X̃'(J))), but it was abandoned.

Purpose: this sets up the 'paradigm' structure attached to a curve or variety with boundary and marked points. The structure is the profinite extension E', with inertia data at the boundary and section data at the rational points, all functorial for the semilinear symmetry group. It is the kind of object the Esquisse/Longue Marche program wants to describe purely group-theoretically: anabelian reconstruction and Galois action on π_1 of moduli/P^1 − 3 points with symmetries.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor issue: the Hom-set target should be Hom(𝒢'_j, E') with the condition 'section of E'→𝒢' over 𝒢'_j'. Without that condition the map is not into sections; this is implicit.
Strictly, X̃' is a pro-scheme; X̃'(j) means the set of compatible systems of Q̄-points above j, i.e. a π_1-torsor. This is fine but unstated.
The index notation in (25) mixes J and 𝔍. The family is indexed by points j ∈ J, not subsets.

ideas.what: Extension 1→π_1(X')→E'→𝒢'→1 combining the geometric fundamental group with the full group of semilinear automorphisms of (X, D, J), which maps to Gal(Q̄/Q)
ideas.modern_name: arithmetic fundamental group extended by symmetries (equivariant / orbifold arithmetic π_1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 fundamental exact sequence); symmetric versions used by Ihara, Nakamura, Drinfeld in the Galois–Teichmüller context
ideas.where_published: SGA1 exp. IX (fundamental exact sequence); Esquisse d'un programme (Galois action on fundamental groups of moduli, with symmetries) in spirit

ideas.what: Rational points j give, for each point x̃ above j, a splitting of the extension over the stabilizer 𝒢'_j, equivariantly in x̃
ideas.modern_name: sections associated to rational points (section map of the section conjecture), equivariant version
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), published in Geometric Galois Actions 1 (1997)

ideas.what: Boundary components give Ẑ(1)-twisted inertia homomorphisms T(Q̄)→π_1, equivariant under E' and Γ (previous page, recalled here)
ideas.modern_name: divisorial / cuspidal inertia subgroups with cyclotomic twist
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA1 / Grothendieck–Murre (tame fundamental group); standard in anabelian geometry

missed.claim: A crossed-out formula (26) attempted an 'extended' family of splittings Ψ^ext, from π_1-type data over X̃'(J) into Hom(𝒢', E'), beyond the stabilizers. It is left unformulated. It possibly aims at the full 𝒢' acting on the set of sections, or at tangential base points.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only a minor trace. It hints at an intended equivariant packaging of section data for the whole symmetry group, but it was abandoned and is too fragmentary to reconstruct.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard formalization: a fundamental group extension enlarged by semilinear automorphisms, with inertia at the boundary and sections at rational points. It is notable as an early (c.1980) appearance of the point→section map before the 1983 Faltings letter. However, the construction itself is elementary and well known in anabelian geometry.
transcription_corrections: (25) should read Ψ = (Ψ_j)_{j∈J} : (X̃'(j) → Hom(𝒢'_j, E')), indexed by points j ∈ J. The insertion reads 'et 𝒢'_j le stab. de j dans 𝒢''.
The parenthesis likely reads '(où cette fois E' désigne l'image inverse de 𝒢' ⊂ 𝒢_{X'} dans E_{X'})'.
In I, 'à c. n. [?] lisses' is better read as describing the components D_i (e.g. 'irréductibles' / 'simples'). The 'c.n.' (croisements normaux) reading is uncertain.
Γ = Aut(Q̄/Q) (or Gal) is plausible as written.
The crossed-out block is (26), not part of (25).
